title: Best Fans UK
short: Desk, tower and pedestal fans compared on measured airflow, noise and power use, from a £30 desk fan to battery-powered air circulators.
intro: A fan's real test is how much air it moves and how loud it is doing it. This guide compares fans tested by Expert Reviews, who assembled each one and measured airflow at 1m with a digital anemometer at minimum, medium and maximum settings, sound levels with a decibel meter, and power draw at the highest and lowest speeds. Prices are as reviewed and the guide was updated in September 2026.

products.name: Sefte Pro 10in Pedestal Air Circulator
products.best_for: Buyers who want a powerful, quiet fan they can carry anywhere
products.key_spec: Removable rechargeable battery (32+ hours on medium), 4.6m/s airflow at top speed, 35.5dBA maximum, 1.1m height or 59cm floor fan
products.summary: Expert Reviews' top pick, with a removable, replaceable battery that gave over 32 hours on its medium setting and a modular design that works as a full-height pedestal or a 59cm floor fan. It measured 4.6m/s at top speed and 2.2m/s on its lowest, peaking at 35.5dBA and a virtually silent 24.5dBA on setting one, though at £200 it's expensive.
products.search: Meaco Sefte Pro 10in Pedestal Air Circulator

products.name: DF0030 Tower Fan
products.best_for: Small living rooms and bedrooms on a tight budget
products.key_spec: 30in tower, three speeds, 80° oscillation, integrated carry handle, 45W
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this bargain easy to carry around the house, with decent airflow at each of its three speeds. It cooled a small living room fine and is good for taking heat out of a bedroom before bed, but even on its lowest setting it's far from silent, so it isn't ideal for sleeping.
pros: Easy to move, with a handle
cons: Not silent even on its lowest setting

products.name: Whisper Flex 2
products.best_for: Buyers who want app control, schedules and voice assistant support
products.key_spec: 30 speeds, Night and Natural modes, Wi-Fi app, Alexa and Google Home, 3.5m/s measured
products.summary: One of the cleverest fans Expert Reviews has tested, with 30 speed settings and a Natural mode that varies speed for a convincing breeze. It measured up to 3.5m/s and 45.8dBA at maximum, still far from raucous, with barely audible lower speeds, though the app and fiddly setup process need improving.
pros: Smart features work well: app, schedules, Google Home and Alexa
cons: App and setup process need improvement

products.name: 30in Tower Fan
products.best_for: Buyers who prioritise airflow over noise and features
products.key_spec: 30in tower, three speeds, 60° oscillation, 3.2m/s measured, mechanical timer, 49.9dBA maximum
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this one of the more powerful tower fans tested for the money, reaching 3.2m/s at a metre away and still 2.4m/s on its lowest setting. It's loud though, at 41dB on low and 49.9dB at full, and airflow is strongest low down, but the old-school mechanical timer works well.

products.name: Sefte Pro 10in Table Air Circulator
products.best_for: Buyers who want the most powerful, near-silent desk or table fan
products.key_spec: Removable battery (up to 40 hours quoted), 4.6m/s airflow, 26.4-45.2dBA, 120° oscillation
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this the table fan to beat for performance, with a removable battery for a take-anywhere floor or table fan. It measured up to 4.6m/s with sound as low as 26.4dBA and no louder than 45.2dBA, though it's a bit bulky for some surfaces (the smaller 8in model suits those).
cons: Too big for some desks and surfaces
products.search: Meaco Sefte Pro 10in Table Air Circulator

products.name: Pedestal Air Circulator
products.best_for: Light sleepers who want strong airflow and a proper Sleep mode
products.key_spec: 12 speeds, 4.3m/s max, oscillates horizontally and vertically, Sleep mode, 35.8dB at halfway
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this among the more powerful fans tested, reaching 4.3m/s, but quiet enough at lower settings to doze comfortably: 2.5m/s at a mere 35.8dB halfway. A sensible Sleep mode steps the speed down every 30 minutes and the build is rock solid, though at top speed it reaches 48dB.

products.name: Ion Fresh Cooling Tower Fan
products.best_for: Living rooms where looks and controlled airflow matter more than silence
products.key_spec: 1.07m tower, built-in ioniser, 7° tilt, 70° oscillation, 2.3m/s measured, 41-50dB
products.summary: Expert Reviews liked the well-controlled airflow, classy brushed-copper finish, tilt feature and bundled remote, and found it made stuffy rooms more liveable. It measured 2.3m/s at maximum and 1.3m/s at its lowest, but it's not ideal for sleeping, at 41dB even at its quietest and 50dB at its worst.
pros: Well-controlled airflow with a wide 70° sweep
Timer, sleep and natural modes plus remote

products.name: HT 900E TurboForce
products.best_for: Maximum cooling power for a small desk on a small budget
products.key_spec: 40W turbo motor, 2.7m/s measured, 90° tilting head, wall-mountable, 47.5dBA maximum
products.summary: Expert Reviews called this a monster for a budget desk fan, with 2.7m/s gusts strong enough to send papers flying, plus a tilting head that also allows wall mounting. Construction is rock solid, but at medium or high speed it makes 'an unholy racket', reaching 47.5dB, and it's a bearable 40dB on low.

products.name: 36in Tower Fan
products.best_for: Larger living rooms wanting an efficient, well-built tower
products.key_spec: 36in tower, 3.2-3.3m/s measured, Auto and Sleep modes, 1-12 hour timer, about 20W on lower settings
products.summary: Expert Reviews found this efficient way to cool a large area: 3.2m/s at top speed, 3.3m/s in Turbo, and 2.1m/s at around 32dB on its next-to-lowest setting, almost whisper quiet. It's well built with no wobble, has an Auto mode that follows room temperature, and uses only about 20W on lower settings, though it's loud at its highest speeds (44.4-45.2dB).
pros: Cools large areas with little fuss
Auto and Sleep modes plus timer

guide.q: Will a fan actually cool my room?
guide.a: A fan pushes air around rather than cooling it, so it won't cool a room as well as an air conditioner. Expert Reviews notes fans are far cheaper to buy and run, and with the UK's comparatively mild, dry summers, an air conditioning unit may be overkill anyway.

guide.q: Desk fan, pedestal fan or tower fan?
guide.a: A desk fan (£20-£50, like the Honeywell here) only cools a desk-sized space. A pedestal fan is larger and more powerful for bigger spaces but bulky, and its height, pivot and oscillation are adjustable. A tower fan, like the Levoit or Dimplex here, gives near-pedestal cooling in a slimmer form, with less adjustability.

guide.q: How noisy is too noisy for sleeping?
guide.a: Expert Reviews' rule of thumb: 35-40dB is quiet, 40-45dB is bearable, and above 45dB is too loud to sleep peacefully. Always use the lower speed settings, and consider a fan with a Sleep mode, like the Princess here, which reduces speed every 30 minutes.

No. Even the most powerful fans tested use around 40W at maximum, and the most efficient use under 20W at full blast and less than 5W at their lowest. Using the timer, a temperature-sensing Auto mode or a Sleep mode keeps costs down further.
